column1: # Entry-point documentation, extracted from the LY_DEFINE and
# Upstream registers these from the macro into a hash table
# hands to scm/document-functions.scm. The port's entry points are C#
# lambdas with nowhere to carry a docstring, so the data is carried here and
# The arglist is stringified as the C preprocessor would leave #ARGLIST:
# every run of whitespace collapsed to one space. \n is a newline.
# THREE RULES DECIDE WHAT IS IN HERE, and each was added because taking the
# source at face value put something in the generated manual that the oracle
#   * A docstring may be a C++ RAW STRING LITERAL WITH A NON-EMPTY DELIMITER,
#     R"delim( ... )delim", which is how LilyPond writes any docstring that
#     contains a quotation mark. Reading only R"( ... )" leaves 'delim(' in
#     the text and drops every embedded quoted string.
#   * A SMOB TYPE PREDICATE is included only when its class actually derives
#     from a smob base (class OR struct -- Duration and Tuplet_description are
#     structs). Smob_base<T>::init() defines the predicate, so a class that
#     merely declares type_p_name_ never gets one: lily/include/box.hh does
#     exactly that, and the oracle answers #f to (defined? 'ly:box?).
#   * An entry point behind a build flag the oracle build does not set is
#     skipped -- #if GS_API, which is why ly:gs-api and ly:shutdown-gs are

Create a moment with rational main timing @var{m}, and optional grace timing
@var{g}.

A @dfn{moment} is a point in musical time.  It consists of a pair of rationals
@w{(@var{m}, @var{g})}, where @var{m} is the timing for the main notes, and
@var{g} the timing for grace notes.  In absence of grace notes, @var{g}@tie{}is
zero.

For compatibility reasons, it is possible to write two numbers specifying
numerator and denominator instead of the rationals.  These forms cannot be
mixed, and the two-argument form is disambiguated by the sign of the second
argument: if it is positive, it can only be a denominator and not a grace
timing.
